CarPlay entitlement vs CarPlay product-page localization

Teams conflate two separate problems after shipping a CarPlay app:

CarPlay entitlement (engineering + Apple approval)

You request CarPlay capability in the Apple Developer portal, implement CPTemplateApplicationScene or audio/navigation CarPlay templates, pass App Review, and receive entitlement approval. That unlocks the in-car experience inside supported vehicles — it does not auto-fill Simplified Chinese on your App Store product page.

CarPlay product-page metadata (App Store Connect copy)

When your app supports CarPlay, Connect exposes a CarPlay product page under the zh-Hans localization row: name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and in-car screenshot slots with optional overlay captions. Buyers evaluating CarPlay apps on the China storefront see this page — with dash UI captures showing navigation lists, audio controls, parking timers, or EV charge status. Each field you leave blank or in English can surface Latin script even when entitlement is approved and the iPhone listing reads native.

AppLocale covers the second problem only. We do not file entitlement requests, audit CarPlay UI templates, license map tiles, or modify your Xcode CarPlay target.

What China CarPlay buyers see when metadata is still English

Drivers and passengers in China browse CarPlay-enabled apps from the App Store before pairing in a vehicle. Common failure modes when only the iPhone row is zh-Hans:

  • English in-car screenshot captions — overlay lines on dash captures still read "CarPlay", "Drive", or US marketing slogans under a Chinese subtitle
  • Untranslated CarPlay keywords — the 100-character keyword field on the CarPlay tab left empty or still en-US while iPhone keywords are Chinese
  • English description on the CarPlay tab — long listing body still mirrors your US page word-for-word when buyers expand the in-car product page
  • Latin road-name overlays — navigation screenshots show English street labels in burned-in or Connect caption fields
  • Audio now-playing lines in English — dash captures display Latin track or station names in overlay text meant for marketing
  • Assumed inheritance — team saved zh-Hans on the iPhone media manager but never opened the CarPlay tab and clicked Save
  • Entitlement done, metadata skipped — CarPlay works in a test vehicle but the China storefront CarPlay page was never filled

Better zh-Hans CarPlay metadata reduces friction when buyers evaluate in-car apps — it does not replace in-car UI localization inside the binary, dash screenshot re-export, map data licensing, or Apple review decisions.

Common mistakes on CarPlay zh-Hans listings

  • Only localizing the iPhone screenshot set — in-car CarPlay captures in the CarPlay matrix still show English overlay lines from the en-US primary locale
  • Reusing iPhone captions on dash frames — phone tap-and-swipe phrasing does not describe steering-wheel or dash workflows visible in CarPlay art
  • Skipping the CarPlay tab entirely — Connect does not auto-populate in-car media or listing fields from iPhone uploads

What good zh-Hans CarPlay listing copy looks like

CarPlay product-page copy should name what the driver or passenger experiences on the dash — not a copy-paste of iPhone slogans:

  • Name and subtitle — concise Chinese that matches how buyers search for in-car navigation, audio, parking, or EV tools; avoid English codenames unless trademark requires them
  • Keywords — hanzi queries for CarPlay-adjacent use cases within the 100-character cap; not romanization or English category words alone
  • Description — plain-language paragraphs on dash workflows: hands-free navigation, steering-wheel controls, offline maps, charging-station filters — within Connect character limits
  • Promotional text — one timely hook within the 170-character cap when you maintain CarPlay-specific promo messaging
  • In-car screenshot captions — one outcome per dash frame: turn-by-turn clarity, playlist browsing on the dash, parking spot countdown, EV range planning — not generic "better driving experience" filler
  • Dash-appropriate phrasing — describe glanceable, voice-friendly workflows instead of phone pinch gestures when the screenshot shows CarPlay chrome
  • Voice match — same 你/您 and punctuation habits as your zh-Hans iPhone description and description field

zh-Hans in-car captions can differ idiomatically from en-US lines when the on-screen feature is the same — avoid mirroring comma-heavy English brochure phrasing onto dash UI art.
